patients.label: 85-year-old man with diabetes and oxalate nephropathy with acute kidney injury after a juice diet during treatment for upper gastrointestinal bleeding

identity_evidence.quote: An 85-year-old man presented to the Department of Nephrology

attribution_limitations: The Discussion says "it was tested in our patient only 10 days after stopping juices". The immediately preceding sentence is about oxalate excretion and glomerular filtration, not a named test; the 24-hour urine oxalate is named two sentences earlier, so the pronoun is not a literal adjacent-sentence back-reference, and the juice stop date is not otherwise stated. No time is attached to the urine oxalate fact.
The authors state the patient was expected to have only a slow recovery or become dependent on dialysis; this is an expectation with two alternatives, not an observed outcome.

Acute tubular necrosis and volume depletion are stated as likely contributors, not confirmed diagnoses; the Figure 1b caption separately describes histologic changes of acute tubular necrosis, recorded as a pathology observation.
The source prints "peak creatine" where the peak value of the serially reported creatinine is described.

The pomegranate juice intake is described as three to four times daily in the case and as approximately 600-900 mL per day in the Discussion; the serving size is not stated, and the approximately 450 mg/day vitamin C figure is the authors' estimate.

The abstract and introduction say he was "put on" or "kept on" a juice diet, while the case says he was advised a semi-solid diet and preferred a liquid diet for a week; the source does not say whether the week-long liquid diet is the same intake as the pomegranate juice reported on questioning.
The ultrasonography sentence closes the paragraph about the previous hospital but does not name the hospital where it was done.

Two admissions are described: the creatinine times are anchored to the previous hospital's admission, while the painkiller denial and dialysis start are anchored to admission to the authors' hospital.

He preferred a liquid diet for a week.
